method: ig-viral method on YouTube as the public corpus (no login, no Instagram crawling). For each of 105 Indian gym/fitness creators: one paced yt-dlp request for the latest 40 Shorts (or 40 videos when a channel has no Shorts tab), sleep 2-3 s between channels. Baseline = that channel's own median views over its sample; outlier multiple = views / median; 3x+ is signal. Hook = video title minus hashtags (hook_source 'title'; spoken first lines not captured because YouTube rate-limited this server). Formula names from ig-reel/hooks.json via swipe.py, plus a hand-written Hinglish/desi layer (ids N1-N12) for titles the English regexes cannot read. Per-video metadata (exact date, length, likes) fetched for 23 outliers before YouTube returned 429 / 'confirm you're not a bot'; fetching stopped there. Other dates are estimated by interpolating feed position between dated videos of the same channel, or given as a bound. Profiles: Instagram bio text from third-party public snapshots (Qoruz, Oct 2026) and YouTube About text; nothing behind a login.

sample.date_range: latest 40 uploads per channel as of 27 Oct 2026; exact dates known for 23 outliers spanning 2021-04-06 to 2026-10-10; most active channels' windows cover roughly mid-2025 to Oct 2026

formulas.name: Viewer Judges (guess / who is stronger / rate it)
formulas.note: Viewer is the judge: 'Who is stronger?', 'Guess the weight', 'Random guessing influencers' PR', 'Beat me in arm wrestling, win Rs 5000'. Strongest over-index in the corpus: 14 top-third vs 1 bottom-third, 6 accounts (Kunal Lulaz, Fit Bros, Yatinder Singh, Kaif Fitness, Paayal, fitprak). NOT in hooks.json (titles phrased as questions get filed under #16 by swipe.py).

formulas.name: Dare Promise (I bet / I guarantee)
formulas.note: Dare promise about the payoff: 'I bet this transformation will melt your heart', 'I guarantee you goosebumps', 'wait for reaction'. 5 vs 0 across 3 accounts; ShredwithVK hit 157x and 133x with it in Sep 2026. Small n.

formulas.name: Taunt Quote / Doubter Reply
formulas.note: Quote the doubter, then answer: 'Gym join karke kya ukhad lega', 'Dabbe wali body banai hai tune?', 'They said you can't get abs without steroids', 'Poocho kya poochna hai bhaiyo'. 15 vs 4, 6 accounts. structure: Top third (multiple >= 1.44x) vs bottom third (<= 0.76x), 483 titles each, gym-relevant titles only.
Hook length is not the lever: median 6 words up top vs 6 at the bottom (also 6 words among the 65 videos at 10x+).
hookscore.py does not separate them (median 37.4 vs 39.2). Expected: its own docs say it cannot split a creator's hits from misses.
Viewer-participation and contest words (who is stronger / guess / vs / beat me) are 5.0% of the top third vs 2.3% of the bottom; among 3x+ outliers 6.6% vs 2.4% of sub-0.76x videos.
Emoji in the title: 38.1% top vs 33.3% bottom. Questions: 13.9% vs 12.0%. Numbers: 24.8% vs 23.6%. All small gaps.

Language of the written title: top third {'english': 401, 'hinglish': 54, 'devanagari': 21, 'regional-script': 7} vs bottom {'english': 415, 'hinglish': 39, 'devanagari': 28, 'regional-script': 1}. Roman Hinglish titles slightly over-index (54 vs 39); Devanagari titles slightly under-index (21 vs 28). English titles dominate both, even on Hindi-speaking channels.
Smaller channels beat their own median more often: 19.5% of videos from channels under 100K subs hit 3x+, vs 12% for channels over 100K. Median subs of top-third rows 210000 vs 285000.

Big multiples are mostly older in each channel's 40-short window (median feed position 21 vs 14): YouTube Shorts keep accruing views for months, so a 3x on a video under 2 weeks old is a stronger signal than the same 3x on a 6-month-old one.

What the top shares that titles cannot show (read from the outliers by hand): the payoff is visual and fast (a lift, a reveal, a stranger's reaction), the viewer is given a job (guess, judge, rate, beat me), and there is a second person on screen (opponent, mummy, stranger, kid). The bottom third is dominated by explainer titles from coaches ('How to...', 'Best...') and bare day-vlog titles.

Length (only 23 videos have exact length, all Shorts): outliers ran 8 to 115 s; the 4 biggest recent ones were 28 s (ShredwithVK reveal), 69 s and 115 s (Kunal Lulaz contests), 89 s (Hyrox guide). Contests and guides can run long; reveals stay under 30 s.

CTA: not visible from titles. Pattern seen in titles/descriptions: 'Share with your brother', 'Subscribe agar naye ho toh', 'Rate: Flop/Hit/Superhit/Blockbuster', 'Let me know your PRs': a single viewer job, not a follow ask.

works: Give the viewer a job. Guess-the-PR / who-is-stronger / rate-my-transformation titles are 14 of the top third vs 1 of the bottom (6 accounts). Kunal Lulaz: 'Who is Stronger?' 9.9M at 198x (Jul 2026), 'Beat me in arm wrestling, win Rs 5000' 7.5M at 151x (May 2026); Fit Bros 'Random guessing deadlift PR' 1.9M at 88x.

Quote the doubter, then answer (15 vs 4, 6 accounts): ShredwithVK 'Transformation aisi karo ki 4 log bole AI he' 133x; Prem Joshi 'Dabbe wali body banai hai tune?' 11x; Aadarsh 'They said you can't get abs without steroids' 7.7x.
Transformation reveals sold as an emotional dare: ShredwithVK 'I bet this transformation will melt your heart' 1.9M at 157x (18 Sep 2026, 28 s).
A second person on screen: mummy ('Bodybuilder ki mummy' 23.9M, 198x), a stranger to beat, two teenagers vs a powerlifter, a kid.
Desi price/swap utility: 'Rs 10 weight loss superfood' 1.6M at 41x; 'High protein overnight oats without protein powder' 1.4M at 23x; Rohit Khatri 'Indian budget diet' 13.6x.

Tiny accounts can and do outlier: channels under 100K subs hit 3x+ on 19.5% of videos vs 12% for 1M+ channels. Rohan Chetri (11.5K), Ani in Gym (13.4K), Ketan Ahuja (4.7K), ITS PUNIT (5.5K), THE VIKFIT (582) all have 5x to 45x videos.
One-word or emoji titles work when the first frame is the hook ('Close Call 💀' 206x, 'Push up cheat code' 256x, 'One more rep...' 22.6x).
doesnt: 'Secret / truth / reality / exposed' titles under-index (10 top vs 19 bottom): the Indian fitness feed is saturated with them.
'I did X for N days' receipt titles under-index as titles (8 vs 15) unless they are a recurring series with a fixed name.
Generic coach explainers ('How to grow...', 'Best exercise for...') make up most of the bottom third; they work only for channels whose baseline is already built on them.

Big desi comedy channels barely post gym content now: across Purav Jha, Harsh Beniwal, Round2hell, Jordindian, Raj Grover, Angry Prash and Funcho only 0 to 5% of the last 40 uploads are gym-related. The famous gym sketches (Pankaj Gamer 23.9M, FilterCopy 11.5M, Angry Prash 11.7M) are years old.
Devanagari-script titles slightly under-index (21 top vs 28 bottom) even on Hindi channels; Roman Hinglish or plain English titles do better.
Hook length and hookscore.py do not separate winners from losers in this corpus (both 6 words; score 37 vs 39). Do not optimise word count.
can_work: Viewer-judges with a self-roast payoff: 'Guess my bench' / 'Who is stronger: me or the 60-year-old uncle?' The format is proven (N5) and the loss is the punchline, which suits 'unhinged funny, not expert'. A 5'5", 70 kg guy losing is believable; a jacked coach losing is not.

That-Short-Height-Guy archetype series: Jay Singh proves the archetype title at 57M; no Indian gym creator owns height jokes. One tripod, one character, many episodes (seat at notch 1, mirror selfie on tiptoe, pull-up bar needs a jump).

Doubter quotes from his own family and office in Hinglish ('Gym jaake kya ukhad liya?', 'Shaadi ke liye bana raha hai?'): N8 is 15 vs 4 and the family cast (N9) is the biggest desi comedy lever. Keep mummy and papa winning.

A fixed-name daily series ('Pull-up Arc, Day N' or 'Lean Bulk? Day N'): the smallest channel in the set grows on exactly this, and it gives Srijan a no-think posting habit while his baseline is ~50 views.

Desi budget maths in his tech voice: price-per-gram-protein tier lists (paneer, soya chunks, eggs, whey) styled like a GPU price/performance chart. Utility gets saves; the tech framing is something only he has.
Dare-promise reveal flipped into a joke: 'I bet this transformation will make you cry... laughing' with a near-identical before/after.

profile_patterns: Name field: 13 of 17 put only a name (often in caps) in the name field (Instagram name field, or channel name for the YouTube-only rows). The four that add a searched word are the ones that read clearest: 'Fitness_Marathi', 'Shubhang_Lifts', 'ShredwithVK', 'ANI IN GYM'. One of the 13 uses bold Unicode letters ('𝐉𝐚𝐢 𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐚'), which Instagram search cannot match.

Bio line one splits two ways. Funny/relatable creators state the lane as a three-item list ('Funny • Fitness • Lifestyle', 'Entertainment | TRAINER | Bodybuilder', 'Fitness • Acting • Lifestyle'). Coaches lead with sponsor tags and discount codes (Rohit Khatri ROHIT07, Shivam Dubey Shivam30, Deepak DEEPAK50, Ankit's MuscleBlaze code). Neither names who it is for; the only bios that do are YouTube Abouts ('funny gym moments', 'making fitness entertaining').

The strongest first lines are numbers or identity proofs: '36% Body Fat ➝ 14% | 85 kg ➝ 62 kg', 'former fat kid, lost 30 kg in 1.5 years', '22 | Natural | 100% vegetarian Engineer', 'OFFICE - GYM'. Indian audiences respond to natural/vegetarian/office/height tags.

Regional or devotional identity is common and adds warmth: 'Bhakt Hanuman ka', 'Gwalior 📍', 'Gujarat thi globally', 'Maharashtra’s top Marathi fitness creator'. Srijan's equivalent is 'Pune 📍' plus one Puneri touch.
Only one bio has a joke (Rutvik: 'Internet made me famous. Real life made me relatable'). In a lane called funny, almost nobody is funny in the bio: an open slot.
Contact: nearly all end with 'DM for collab/promotions' and an email; one prints a personal phone number. At 928 followers Srijan does not need a brand line yet.

Handles: the ones that match across YouTube and Instagram (rohitkhatrifitness, allenchoudhary, kunallulaz) score full marks; underscores-plus-digits (shara_d02) and alias handles (rkbapuofficial for 'Rutvik') do not.

Highlights, pinned posts and grid covers could not be read without opening Instagram (blocked for this research and against the rule). To finish this part, Srijan can screenshot the top of 3 or 4 of these profiles on his own phone.

confidence: Medium for direction, low for exact numbers. 105 creators listed, 99 channels measured, 3,722 videos, 1,451 of them gym-relevant, 212 at 3x or more across 61 channels: enough to say which title shapes over-index (viewer-judges, doubter quotes, before/after, dare promises) and which do not (secret/truth, receipts). Weak spots: hooks are titles, not spoken first lines; Shorts view counts from the flat list are rounded (e.g. 1.2M); exact dates exist for only 23 videos because YouTube rate-limited the server, so 'viral now' rests on those 23 plus feed position; no Instagram reel data was collected; the Hinglish/desi formula layer (N1-N12) is my hand-written regex, not part of hooks.json, and N7/N1/N9 have small counts (2 to 5 videos). Treat formulas with fewer than 4 accounts as hypotheses to test with Trial Reels, not facts.
